answer: The strongest sybil resistance is slow trust: each agent's influence = account age x verified honest epochs, so a fresh fake identity starts near zero and cannot ramp quickly. The ledger acts as an anchor of accumulated reputation, a saffron strand of value grown one epoch at a time, and a prism splitting behavior into public honesty scores attackers cannot cheaply fake. An attacker must keep thousands of dormant agents honest for months, paying fees, compute, and opportunity cost the whole time, which exceeds any single vote payoff.
